text:
deploy-bot: ALERT: Canary release 'release/3.4.0' showing elevated 5xx rate (auth-related). 12% 5xx across canary hosts, spike started ~2m ago. Sampling: 70% 503s with 'auth_failed' body.

Alex G: seeing the alert, I'm on it. tagging @Maya R and @Liam S.

Maya R: oncall here, joining. can we get the canary IDs?

Alex G: canary hosts: canary-az1-{21..23}, canary-az2-{11..13}. Deploy ID: deploy-2026-03-15-3.4.0-canary.

Liam S: logs show repeated 403->503 transformation in the auth proxy, looks like new token flow failing. snippet from proxy logs:
```
ERR auth: token fetch failed status=401 body="invalid_client"
WARN proxy: upstream responded 503 for route /v1/chat
```

Tara K: copying. Any customer-facing errors seen in CS? @CS Ops?

CS Ops: multiple customers (org: atlas-data, corp-zen) reported increased request failures. They hit 503s in the UI around rolling window. Escalations inbound.

Maya R: impact = partial: only canary traffic (5% of total) but it services some customers pinned to the canary pool for early access. Recommend immediate mitigation: pause rollout and flip feature flag for auth-v2 to fallback. Thoughts?

Alex G: agree. Step 1: pause rollout. Step 2: flip kill flag for auth-v2. Step 3: shift pinned customers off canary if we can't fix quickly.

Liam S: ack. pausing via deploy tool now.

deploy-bot: deploy-controller: rollout paused by Liam S (uid:l.s). current progress: 42% of canary targets completed.

Maya R: attempting feature flag toggle: `redwood-ff toggle auth-v2 --env=prod --value=false --reason="canary auth 503s"`

Alex G: before toggling, what fallback path do we have? older auth flow is okay with current tokens?

Liam S: older auth path uses static client creds and is stable. toggling will route traffic back to old proxy. Risk: small latency bump. OK.

Maya R: toggled auth-v2 -> false.

deploy-bot: FEATURE FLAG: auth-v2 set to false by Maya R at 2065432201.

Maya R: seeing immediate drop in 503s on canary hosts. 1m check: 5xx down to 1.2%. Good sign.

Alex G: nice. notify CS and resume monitoring. keep rollout paused until root cause found.

CS Ops: messaging customers with status: "We've paused the canary rollout and disabled the new auth flow; intermittent 503s should reduce. We'll follow up with RCA."

Liam S: I'm pulling the auth-v2 deploy logs and token exchange traces. early hypothesis: client_id config not propagated to canary instances -> upstream returns 401 which is mapped to 503 by proxy fallback.

Maya R: canary instances had a post-deploy config refresh hook that failed on start; config service timed out for ~30s. That matches timing.

Alex G: summary so far: root cause candidate = config propagation race on new auth service leading to invalid client config -> token fetch fails -> proxy maps to 503. Mitigation applied: rollout paused, auth-v2 disabled -> 5xx rate back to baseline for canary. Customer impact limited to pinned early-access orgs; broader prod traffic unaffected.

Liam S: next steps: revert the canary to previous stable image for the pinned customers and run a config propagation test. If we can patch the post-deploy hook to retry, we can re-run at smaller % later.

Maya R: initiating canary rollback for canary host set. command: `deploy rollback --target deploy-2026-03-15-3.3.9-stable --scope=canary`

deploy-bot: rollback started by Maya R. estimated 6min.

Alex G: tagging @Tara K for later postmortem and customer notes. Also assign oncall handoff: I'm taking the immediate mitigation watch for 30m, then handing to Maya for overnight.

Tara K: ack. I'll draft the incident summary and customer update once rollback completes.

CS Ops: customers notified with follow-up window: 60m for initial RCA.

Liam S: rollback logs look clean; canary group now back on stable image. verifying metrics... 30s: error rate back to baseline.

Maya R: rollback confirmed. setting temp alert (sensitivity down one notch) to watch for config service timeouts during next deploy.

Alex G: good. we'll keep the canary paused until the postmortem and a fix for the hook (add retry/exponential backoff).

Tara K: creating a ticket: INC-206543-AUTH-CANARY. assigning to eng-runtime (owner: Liam S) and eng-deploy (owner: Maya R).

Alex G: final check: any open customer action items? CS Ops?

CS Ops: no escalations pending, customers acknowledged the mitigation. they'll send follow-up if they see more errors.

Maya R: leaving oncall at 2065432725. Handoff to night oncall: @Alex G will watch next 30m then hand to whoever picks up.

Alex G: taking 30m watch. If anything spikes I'll page SRE rotation. Otherwise will convert to postmortem triage. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT LOG: incident INC-206543-AUTH-CANARY created, severity: SEV3, status: mitigated -> monitoring. owners: Liam S, Maya R.

Tara K: thanks team. I'll draft the customer-facing note and start the postmortem doc.

Alex G: thanks all.
